extraction.name: ChartQA: A Benchmark for Question Answering about Charts with Visual and Logical Reasoning
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark covering 9.6K human-written questions as well as 23.1K questions generated from human-written chart summaries, focusing on visual and logical reasoning over charts.
extraction.creator: Ahmed Masry, Do Xuan Long, Jia Qing Tan, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Charts were crawled from four different online sources: Statista, Pew Research, Our World In Data (OWID), and OECD. For Pew, only chart images were crawled. For the other three, underlying data tables, metadata, SVG files, and associated text descriptions were extracted. Human-authored QA pairs were collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk, and machine-generated QA pairs were created using a T5 model fine-tuned on SQuAD and applied to human-written chart summaries from Statista.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Chart images and underlying data tables/metadata from Statista, Pew Research, Our World In Data, and OECD.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Machine-generated questions were filtered using a heuristic to remove invalid questions where the answer could not be found in the chart data table. The test set of the machine-generated dataset was manually cleaned by removing invalid questions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Underlying data tables were extracted from chart images using an adapted ChartOCR model. Visual features were extracted using neural models (Mask R-CNN). Questions and answers were validated for correctness. Data was split into train, validation, and test sets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human-authored QA pairs were created by Amazon Mechanical Turk workers who wrote compositional and visual questions for each chart. Each question was answered by two workers; if answers matched exactly, it was considered correct. Otherwise, manual checking was performed. Machine-generated questions were created by fine-tuning a T5 model on SQuAD and applying it to human-written chart summaries from Statista.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Agreement between crowd workers based on exact matches was 61.04%. When considering typos and lexical variations, agreement was 78.55% based on a manual check of 500 random samples.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers with an acceptance rate of 95% and at least 5000 accomplished HITs. Workers were selected via a pretest.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: T5 model, ChartOCR, Mask R-CNN, CRAFT
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to help users analyze data and make informed decisions by answering complex reasoning questions about charts. However, models can be abused to mislead the public about chart content and implications.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset contains charts from four sources with diverse topics, but Politics is a common topic, particularly in the Pew dataset (45.4% of charts). Bar charts are the most common type. The dataset may exhibit biases present in the source data (e.g., US Politics in Pew).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Existing models struggle with nested arithmetic operations, complex visual compositional questions requiring multi-stage reasoning, and OCR noise. Performance decreases when gold data tables are not provided. The dataset is limited to bar, line, and pie charts. Machine-generated questions may still contain invalid or unanswerable questions if not filtered.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning of Question Answering models involving visual and logical reasoning over charts.
